question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed sessions to request ACP host or worker spawns, and which security boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The code can implement several shapes, but the real decision is whether OpenClaw should preserve a strict sandbox boundary, add an audited host bridge, or route ACP into isolated workers; automation should not choose that trust model.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and cleanup boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn/steer/cancel APIs, allowlisting, rate limits, and durable audit logs for operators who accept controlled privilege escalation.

options.title: Keep The Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions must use runtime="subagent" or run ACP-capable harnesses inside the container until a stronger security design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and cleanup boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz merged the current ACP sandbox-inheritance hardening and has adjacent ACP/acpx runtime history, making this the best available routing signal for the trust-boundary decision.
